note: Theseus carries off the child Helen and hides her at Aphidnae — the bride the Dioscuri reclaim and Paris will one day take to Troy.
Come down for Cerberus on his last labour, Heracles finds the bound comrades and raises Theseus from the Chair of Forgetfulness.
The same death told in two arms: Deianira's shirt steeped in Nessus' blood consumes Heracles on the pyre.
At Knossos the labyrinth Daedalus built for Minos holds the Minotaur Theseus comes to slay.
Theseus flees Crete with Ariadne and puts in at Dia — where Dionysus takes her and the black sail sends Aegeus to his death.
Medea of Colchis, fled from Jason, reaches Aegeus' Athens and all but poisons the arriving Theseus.
Seeking news of his father, Telemachus comes to sandy Pylos to the old charioteer Nestor — the one captain who reached home unharmed.
From Pylos Telemachus rides to Sparta, where Menelaus tells of Proteus and the long road back from Egypt.
Orpheus' counter-melody lets the Argo pass the Sirens when Butes alone swims to their isle.
Like Theseus and Pirithous, Orpheus descends alive to Hades — but charms the rulers of the dead with song rather than force.
Actaeon son of Aristaeus and Autonoe, bred by Chiron to the chase, is torn by his own hounds on Cithaeron — the grief that drives his father from Greece.
Long-haired Aristaeus weds Autonoe in the Cadmean house — binding the bee-keeper's craft to the royal line of Cadmus and Harmonia.
Apollodorus cites Acusilaus: Zeus destroyed Actaeon because he wooed Semele — one of three rival charges against Cadmus' hunter-grandson.
Odysseus questions Tyro first among the heroines — she declares herself daughter of noble Salmoneus.
Pelops bears the ivory shoulder from the gods' feast; his sister Niobe will boast against Leto from the same doomed lineage.
Zetes and Calais drive the Harpies from blind Phineus' table; Iris swears by Styx, and the seer foretells the Symplegades for Jason's crew.
Danaus flees Egypt for Argos, the land of his ancestress Io — the wandering cow whose line the fifty brides will crown and curse.
When Zeus carries Europa to Crete, Agenor sends Cadmus to bring her back — the sister's abduction that sends the brother to Apollo's cow and the dragon of Thebes.
Semele and Pentheus belong to the Cadmean house — Dionysus is twice-born from a Theban princess and returns to shatter the king who denied him.
Theseus abandons Ariadne on Dia; Dionysus takes her from the shore — the Cretan princess passes from the Attic hero to the wine-god.
Odysseus sees Tantalus, Sisyphus, and Tityus in violent torment as he passes through the house of Hades — the same eternal punishments catalogued in Tartarus.
Persephone sends up the shades of famous heroines to Odysseus' pit of blood — the queen of the dead who rules beside Pluto in the rape-and-return myth.
Caeneus the invulnerable Lapith — once the woman Caenis — kills many centaurs at Peirithous' wedding before the survivors bury him under massy pines.
Ovid tells how Circe poisoned the maiden Scylla into the dog-girt cliff-monster Homer placed opposite Charybdis — not the Scylla of Megara in `scylla-minos`.
The same Circe who turned Odysseus' scouts to swine on Aeaea later scorned Picus in Laurentine Latium and changed him into the woodpecker king.
In the Metamorphoses inset sung by Orpheus, Apollo's discus kills Hyacinthus and the god's grief turns Cyparissus into the cypress — two loves of Phoebus in the same book.
The wedding the gods attended on the Cadmea ends in Illyrian exile — the same founders who sowed the dragon's teeth are turned to crested serpents when the cursed house is done with them.
The seer Hera blinded for siding with Zeus is the same prophet who names Oedipus as the pollution when plague strikes the seven-gated city.
Blinded in life but endowed with prophecy by Zeus, Tiresias alone keeps understanding among the dead and counsels Odysseus at the pit of blood.
Odysseus questions Iphimedeia among the heroines — she tells of Otus and Ephialtes, short-lived but tallest of men, whom the son of Leto destroyed before they could storm Olympus.
Like Typhon before them, the Aloadae piled mountains to scale heaven and make war on the immortals — Earth's last revolt broken before the twins reached manhood.
Ganymede is Tros' fairest son; the mares Zeus gave in recompense for the boy Laomedon later cheats Heracles of — the perjury that brings the first sack of Troy.
Both Orion and Tithonus were mortal loves of the Dawn — the hunter slain by Artemis in Ortygia, the Trojan prince snatched to Ethiopia to be lord of her couch.
Eos bore brazen-crested Memnon to Tithonus in Ethiopia — the son who marched to Troy after Penthesilea while the father still kept the Dawn's couch.
Odysseus names Memnon when praising the comeliest men at Troy to Achilles' shade; Antilochus, whom Memnon killed, came among the same heroes in the pit of blood.
Memnon killed Antilochus son of Nestor before the walls — the runner the old charioteer would mourn when he alone reached sandy Pylos with all his company.
Two faces of Dionysus' wandering triumph: Tyrrhenian pirates off the island Icaria, and the gift of wine to Attic Icarius when the god came to Athens.
After spreading wine through Attica, Dionysus returns to his mother's Theban house — where Pentheus denies the god and is torn apart by the maenads.
